 3. The material facts giving rise to this application are, that the assesse is a public limited company and carries on the business of production of telephone sets and other equipments. For the assessment year 1975-76 the assesse filed a return showing an income of Taka 15,45,969.00 which is subject to set-off against losses of the earlier year. In the computation of the profits and gains of the said year the assesse claimed an amount of Taka 3,63,720.00 which was paid as return on Siemen's investment. The assesse also claimed an allowance of Taka 28,02,861.00 paid to the employees on account of house rent, maternity benefit, medical expenses, transport allowance, etc. in addition to salary and bonus which amounted to Taka 32,15,419.00. The Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Dhaka (South) Zone, Dhaka, in his order of assessment treated the payment of Taka 3,63,720.00 on Siemens' investment as share of profit in lieu of dividend on investment of capital at a fixed rate and so disallowed the same. The Deputy Commissioner of Taxes further treated the expenses of Tk. 28,02,861.00 in addition to salary and bonus as perquisites paid to the employees and disallowed the said allowance on the ground that it had exceeded 30% of the salary and bonus under section 10(4)(d) of the Income-tax Act. The said excess disallowed by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes came to Taka 18,38,235.00. The assessee took an appeal therefrom to the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes who maintained the assessment order relating to the disallowance of the amount on Siemens investment and perquisites in excess of 39% of the salary. The unsuccessful assessee then preferifxl a further appeal to the Taxes Appellate Tribunal being ITA No. 1981 of 1980-81. The Tribunal disposed of the said appeal by its order dated 14th July, 1986. The majority members passed an order in favour of the deletion of disallowance of the excess perquisites and the return on Seimens investment. They took the view that "little perquisites or benefits were allowed to the employees of the assesse beyond what were to be treated as 'salary' in terms of Explanation 1 to section 10(4)(d). In the circumstances, the limitation envisaged in section 10(4)(d) shall have no operation in the case of perquisites allowed to the employees of the assesse company in any of the years under consideration." The Appellate Tribunal was also of the view that the authorities below erred in treating the payment made to Siemens' AG as profit in lieu of dividend. The minority view given by one member with regard to the allowance in respect of perquisites was, however, different. He was of the view that the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes was perfectly justified in maintaining the disallowance of excess perquisites as calculated by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes in accordance with the provision laid down in section 10(4)(d) of the Act. In view of the majority decision the appeal was allowed in part.
